steps.say: Conjunctions are joining words. They join two ideas into one longer sentence.
steps.show: I was hot. I had a drink. → I was hot, so I had a drink.

steps.say: And adds an idea. Or gives a choice.
steps.show: rice and fish, rice or noodles

steps.say: But shows a difference or a surprise.
steps.show: It was sunny, but it was cold.

steps.say: Because gives a reason. So gives a result.
steps.show: I ran because I was late. I was late, so I ran.

steps.say: When and if tell us about time, and about what must happen first.
steps.show: When it rains, we stay in. If you ask, I will help.

check.prompt: I was thirsty, ___ I drank some water.

options.why: But shows a surprise. Drinking when thirsty is no surprise.
If means only when something happens.

hints: What happened because I was thirsty?
You need a word that shows a result.
Read the sentence with each word in the gap.
check.explanation: So shows a result. I was thirsty, so I drank some water.

check.prompt: We stayed inside ___ it was raining.

options.why: So gives a result. Staying inside did not cause the rain.
But shows a surprise. Staying in when it rains is not surprising.

hints: You need a word that gives a reason.
Read the sentence aloud with each word.
check.explanation: Because gives the reason: we stayed inside because it was raining.
